rule: Existing public API status is not evidence that a construct is primitive. Every candidate carries a soundness record and at least one eliminability attempt with exact evidence.

primitives.name: Pure typed fold
primitives.rust_type: trait Behavior { type Addr/Msg/Event/Sends/Ph/Error/Birth; fn init; fn step } (crates/behavior/src/behavior.rs:419-431); first-order kernel trait State::handle (behavior.rs:389-410)
primitives.formation_rule: A behavior is a total deterministic fold from exactly one typed Event to Result<Actions, Error>; init runs before mailbox events.
primitives.operational_semantics: One isolated turn: consume one event, produce the complete effect product as data; no effect is performed by construction. Determinism: the behavior is a function of the message history.
laws: One communication at a time (Agha 1986; De Koster-De Meuter 2025 Isolated Turn; Clinger 1981 arrival events)
Deterministic function of the received message sequence (AMST 1997 sec.2)
Behavior domain equation F ~= [M -> (F x P(A x M))] (Clinger 1981 sec.IV.2, OCR-read)

evidence: crates/behavior-testkit/tests/core.rs drives single events and asserts complete Actions values

eliminability.attempted_signature: (B, Event) -> Result<Actions, E> expressed without a transition function

attempts.approach: Express behaviors as pure data (rule tables) interpreted by a generic engine
attempts.code_summary: conceptual: enum Rule; fn interpret(rules, event) — the engine's interpret function is the fold
attempts.obstruction: The transition function reappears as the engine's interpreter; removal moves the primitive rather than eliminating it

eliminability.rationale: The fold IS the actor transition law; every other construct transforms or constrains fold inputs/outputs.
eliminability.mechanical_probe: not applicable (semantic nucleus; no code probe can remove the transition function)

primitives.name: Typed event sums with extraction traits
primitives.rust_type: Closed event enums + trait UserEvent { fn user; fn into_user } (behavior.rs:361-375); lane traits TimeEvent/PeerEvent (protocol.rs:45-64)
primitives.formation_rule: A composed protocol is a closed sum; each variant belongs to exactly one lane; extraction is total and lossless (into_* returns the unchanged event on mismatch).
primitives.operational_semantics: Each wrapper pattern-matches its own lane, forwards the rest; nesting composes sums left-nested with canonical extraction order.
laws: Extraction round-trip: inject then extract is identity
Lane preservation: no event dropped, duplicated, relabeled, or reordered through any supported wrapper nesting

evidence: cross_lane.rs and two_buffer.rs proptests under randomized interleavings

derived_capabilities: all wrapper event lanes (deadline, receive-timeout, peer-observation, shutdown)

eliminability.attempted_signature: Watching<B: Behavior<Msg = M>> taking the user message type directly, nested with Stashing<B>

attempts.approach: Wrappers accept the inner event type directly instead of composing sums
attempts.code_summary: struct Watching<B> { inner: B } with step(e: B::Event) — nesting Watching<Stashing<B>> forces Watching to know Stashing's concrete event type
attempts.obstruction: Wrapper nesting becomes order-locked and each wrapper must special-case every other wrapper's events; extensible composition impossible without sums

attempts.approach: Erased event payload via Box<dyn Any> + downcast
attempts.code_summary: the compile_fail doctest at behavior.rs:412 encodes the erased effect seat
attempts.obstruction: Fails to compile by design (static-dispatch rule); cargo test --doc -p bombay-behavior: 1 passed (compile_fail verified)

eliminability.rationale: Rust has no structural row types; closed sums + extraction traits are the minimal static encoding of extensible typed protocols.
eliminability.mechanical_probe: compiler-verified for the erasure alternative (doctest); direct-event alternative argued at type level

primitives.name: Typed effect products with SendAlgebra monoid
primitives.rust_type: struct Actions<A, Ph, Sends, Birth> { sends, creates, become_ } (behavior.rs:320-325); struct SendProduct<L, R> (behavior.rs:112); trait SendAlgebra { empty; append } (behavior.rs:118-121)
primitives.formation_rule: A transition's effects form a product of independent seats; send seats form a monoid under append with empty unit; per-lane order retained, no cross-lane order.
primitives.operational_semantics: Effects are pure data until interpreted; lanes stay statically disjoint through wrapper composition.
laws: Effect triple send/create/become, unordered across the triple (FMOODS 2002; Thati MS 2001 sec.2.1.1)
Adjacent sends permute; become/send order unobservable (AMST 1997 b5 = b5')

evidence: driver_accumulation.rs (monoid proptest, lossless accumulation through supervising)
validation: cargo nextest run --workspace includes driver_accumulation and error_paths

eliminability.attempted_signature: Actions<A, Ph, Vec<Delivery<A, M>>, Birth> — a single merged send seat replacing SendProduct lanes

attempts.approach: Collapse all send lanes into one Vec<Delivery>
attempts.code_summary: single-lane Actions; service/timer/observation sends share one vector
attempts.obstruction: Out-of-lane sends become representable: a behavior can emit a service request where only user deliveries belong, violating make-illegal-states-unrepresentable; per-lane static typing is lost

eliminability.rationale: Products with a monoid are the minimal lawful composition of independent finite effect sets; the merged-lane counterexample is a static-safety obstruction.
eliminability.mechanical_probe: argument-level semantic counterexample; a compile probe is not applicable because the failure is representability, not a type error

primitives.name: Uninhabited Never seats
primitives.rust_type: Never (uninhabited enum) used for Ph/Error/Out/Child seats (exit.rs; behavior.rs NoBirths Child = Never)
primitives.formation_rule: An empty seat is typed with the uninhabited type, making inhabitants unconstructible.
primitives.operational_semantics: A behavior with Error = Never cannot fail; with Child = Never cannot create; with Ph = Never has no phases — all at compile time.
laws: Uninhabited seats make illegal results unrepresentable (AGENTS.md static rule)

validation: cargo nextest run --workspace includes algebra probes

eliminability.attempted_signature: Acted<A, (), Sends, Birth, ()> — unit type in the error/phase seats

attempts.code_summary: type alias replacing Never with () in error and phase seats
attempts.obstruction: () is inhabited: Err(()) and Goto(()) become constructible, so 'never fails' / 'no phases' are no longer compile-time-true; wrappers would need runtime validation for a statically empty case

eliminability.rationale: Only an uninhabited type makes the empty seat unconstructible; aliases rename () and products/sums add inhabitants.
eliminability.mechanical_probe: type-level argument; the constructibility of Err(()) is directly checkable — scheduled as a mechanical probe (probe crate, expected clean compile demonstrating the hole)

primitives.name: BirthMode creation-capability type function
primitives.rust_type: trait BirthMode { type Child; } with NoBirths (Child = Never) and Births<C> (behavior.rs:290-303)
primitives.formation_rule: Each behavior carries a type-level function computing its creation authority; wrappers compute the composite authority.
primitives.operational_semantics: NoBirths behaviors cannot construct Create values at all; Births<C> behaviors emit Vec<Create<A, C>>.
laws: Creation authority composes through wrapper nesting (join of component authorities)

validation: cargo nextest run --workspace includes algebra probes

eliminability.attempted_signature: struct Actions<A, Ph, Sends, const CAN_CREATE: bool> or trait-bound marker WithBirths

attempts.code_summary: const generic or runtime flag on Actions
attempts.obstruction: Runtime-only: a NoBirths violation would compile and need a runtime check; the static guarantee is lost

attempts.code_summary: separate traits per capability level with bounds on wrapper impls
attempts.obstruction: Marker bounds cannot compute the join of component authorities through wrapper composition; computing it requires an associated type per composite, which is exactly BirthMode

eliminability.rationale: Creation authority is a reusable algebraic capability (FMOODS 2002 enforces actor properties by a type system; BirthMode is Bombay's static analogue).
eliminability.mechanical_probe: type-level argument; join-computation probe scheduled (attempt marker-trait encoding in a probe crate and record the coherence failure)

primitives.name: Non-capturing function-pointer reactions
primitives.rust_type: type Transition<S, A, M, O, Br, E> = fn(&mut S, A, M) -> Acted<...> (behavior.rs:452-456); struct FnState (behavior.rs:456-470); reaction fn pointers in supervising.rs/watching.rs
primitives.formation_rule: Behavior fragments are stored as non-capturing fn pointers: Copy, statically dispatched, allocation-free.
output_types: Acted<A, Never, Vec<Delivery<A, O>>, Br, E>
primitives.operational_semantics: A reaction maps state + address + message to a transition result; no captured environment, hence no hidden state.
laws: No captures => no hidden state => determinism preserved

validation: cargo nextest run --workspace includes the adapter equivalence test

eliminability.attempted_signature: Replace fn pointers with (a) boxed closures Box<dyn Fn...>, (b) generic closure seats, (c) small State/Behavior implementations as reaction objects

attempts.code_summary: reaction: Box<dyn Fn(&mut S, A, M) -> Acted<...>>
attempts.obstruction: Violates the zero-tolerance static-dispatch rule (dyn banned); allocation on a hot path

attempts.code_summary: Supervising<B, S, F: FnMut...> — one generic seat per reaction site
attempts.obstruction: Arity growth beyond the frozen baseline (Supervising pinned at 2); every caller's types infected

attempts.approach: Reaction objects: small State implementations instead of fn pointers
attempts.code_summary: probe scheduled: implement a supervising reaction as a tiny Behavior/State impl and compare API weight and type surface

eliminability.rationale: Provisional: fn pointers are the current minimal static encoding; the reaction-object alternative is not yet mechanically excluded — if the probe shows reaction objects derive the same capabilities with no static loss, P-fnreact demotes to derived.
eliminability.mechanical_probe: SCHEDULED — first elimination experiment (probe crate with path dependency; record exact type signatures and any compiler errors)

primitives.name: Higher-order behavior wrappers (as a category)
primitives.rust_type: At, ReceiveTimeout, Watching, Supervising/Proxy, Shutdown, Stashing, Fsm, Spec (deadlined.rs, receive_timeout.rs, watching.rs, supervising.rs, shutdown.rs, stashing.rs, fsm.rs, spec.rs)
primitives.formation_rule: A wrapper is a typed event/effect transformation Behavior -> Behavior with inner-first init and lane-preserving step.
output_types: composed Behavior with widened Event sum and computed effect/capability seats
primitives.operational_semantics: Each wrapper folds one event, routes its own lane, delegates the rest, and accumulates effects without dropping, duplicating, reordering, relabeling, or reinterpreting lanes.
laws: Lane preservation under all supported mixed nestings (COMPOSE-MIXED)
Initialization order: inner first, then own effects (init_contract.rs 6/6)

validation: cargo nextest run --workspace includes all cited suites

eliminability.attempted_signature: Each concern inlined into user behaviors: fn step handles timer/watch/stash logic directly

attempts.code_summary: user folds re-implement lane routing and replay per behavior
attempts.obstruction: Mixed-nesting guarantees (cross_lane/two_buffer proptests) hold only because wrappers are isolated transformations; inlining leaves no place to state the no-drop/no-dup invariant per concern and duplicates lane logic in every behavior

eliminability.rationale: The wrapper category is the composition mechanism of the calculus; each concrete wrapper is a derived form built from sums/products/fold.
eliminability.mechanical_probe: argument-level (composition-law preservation); the concrete wrappers each carry composition tests as witnesses
